content_voiceover: This slide reproduces the International Consensus Classification, or ICC, entity list for ALL, and while you don't need to memorize every line, you should recognize the pattern. B-ALL with recurrent genetic abnormalities includes the classic translocation entities, BCR-ABL1, KMT2A rearranged, ETV6-RUNX1, and TCF3-PBX1, the ploidy-defined entities, hyperdiploid, low hypodiploid, and near haploid, and less common fusions like IL3-IGH, iAMP21, and rearrangements of MYC, DUX4, MEF2D, ZNF384, NUTM1, and HLF. The BCR-ABL1-like category is split into ABL-class rearranged, JAK-STAT activated, and not-otherwise-specified subtypes. Newer provisional entities added in the ICC include ETV6-RUNX1-like, PAX5-altered, mutated ZEB2 with IGH-CEBPE, ZNF384-rearranged-like, and KMT2A-rearranged-like B-ALL, plus B-ALL with mutated IKZF1 N159Y or mutated PAX5 P80R. On the T-ALL side, the categories are simpler: early T-cell precursor ALL, with or without BCL11B rearrangement, T-ALL not otherwise specified, and a set of provisional entities.
keypoints: Classic B-ALL entities: BCR-ABL1, KMT2A-r, ETV6-RUNX1, TCF3-PBX1
Ploidy entities: hyperdiploid, low hypodiploid, near haploid
T-ALL: early T-cell precursor, NOS, provisional entities
keypoint_voiceover: Group ICC B-ALL entities into buckets: classic fusion-defined subtypes like BCR-ABL1 and KMT2A rearranged, ploidy-defined subtypes like hyperdiploid and hypodiploid, and a growing list of newer fusion and mutation subtypes such as DUX4, MEF2D, and PAX5-altered disease. T-ALL classification stays comparatively simple, centered on early T-cell precursor status.
